title: EDiR Practice Set 2 · abdomen, musculoskeletal and women's imaging
subtitle: Radform original · abbreviated EDiR-style practice · English
disclaimer: Simulacro original de Radform basado en la estructura publicada del EDiR. No contiene preguntas oficiales ni bancos de pago.

questions.question: Which enterography findings suggest active Crohn disease? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: These findings reflect active intestinal inflammation and hypervascularity.

questions.question: Which CT features favour a benign adrenal lesion? Choose all that apply.
options: Low unenhanced attenuation consistent with a lipid-rich adenoma
questions.explanation: Low attenuation, characteristic washout and macroscopic fat can support benign diagnoses.

questions.question: Developmental dysplasia of the hip in a young infant is initially assessed primarily with:
questions.explanation: Ultrasound evaluates the largely cartilaginous infant hip without ionising radiation.

questions.question: Cardiac MRI in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may demonstrate:
options: Asymmetric hypertrophy and late gadolinium enhancement
questions.explanation: CMR characterises ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis.

questions.question: Which Doppler ultrasound findings support testicular torsion? Choose all that apply.
options: Symmetrically increased arterial flow in every case
questions.explanation: Reduced perfusion and progressive morphological change support torsion; preserved flow does not always exclude early/intermittent torsion.

questions.question: MRI findings typical of spondylodiscitis include:
options: Abnormal adjacent vertebral endplates and disc
A normal disc in every case
questions.explanation: Infection commonly involves the disc and adjacent endplates, often with paravertebral inflammatory change.

questions.question: Basal subpleural honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis on HRCT suggests:
questions.explanation: Typical UIP is characterised by basal/subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis and honeycombing.

questions.question: Which statements about iodinated contrast are correct? Choose all that apply.
options: Previous contrast reactions should be reviewed
Contrast should be used for an appropriate clinical indication
Renal function matters in selected at-risk patients
questions.explanation: Contrast administration requires individual assessment of indication, allergy history and relevant renal risk.

cases.title: Extra-axial brain mass
cases.stem: MRI demonstrates an avidly enhancing extra-axial mass with a broad dural attachment.

questions.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: An extra-axial avidly enhancing dural-based mass is typical of a meningioma.

questions.question: Which additional finding would support an extra-axial origin?
options: CSF cleft and inward displacement of cortex
Central diffusion restriction within an acute infarct
questions.explanation: A CSF cleft and displacement rather than infiltration of cortex support an extra-axial lesion.

cases.title: Suspicious thyroid nodule
cases.stem: Thyroid ultrasound shows a markedly hypoechoic solid nodule with irregular margins and punctate echogenic foci.

questions.question: How should this nodule be regarded?
options: Suspicious and requiring risk stratification under the applicable system
questions.explanation: Marked hypoechogenicity, irregular margins and punctate echogenic foci are suspicious features.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate next imaging-related step?
options: Assign a structured ultrasound risk category and use size/clinical context to guide FNA recommendation
questions.explanation: Structured risk stratification and size thresholds guide biopsy recommendations.

cases.title: Blunt splenic trauma
cases.stem: A haemodynamically stable trauma patient has a splenic laceration and a focal arterial contrast blush on CT.

questions.question: The arterial-phase blush most likely represents:
questions.explanation: A focal arterial contrast collection outside normal vessels indicates a vascular injury.

questions.question: In a stable patient, an appropriate management option may be:
options: Splenic artery embolisation according to injury pattern and clinical context
Full-dose anticoagulation because a blush is present
questions.explanation: Angiography and embolisation can support non-operative splenic preservation in selected stable patients.

questions.question: Which reporting error would be potentially unsafe?
options: Failing to mention obvious active arterial bleeding
questions.explanation: Omission of active bleeding can delay haemostatic treatment.

cases.title: Complex adnexal mass
cases.stem: A postmenopausal woman has a complex adnexal mass on ultrasound and MRI.

questions.question: Which feature most increases suspicion for malignancy?
questions.explanation: Enhancing solid tissue and papillary projections are suspicious features.

questions.question: Ascites and peritoneal implants should:
options: Increase concern for advanced malignant disease
questions.explanation: Ascites with peritoneal implants indicates possible peritoneal dissemination.

questions.question: Which interpretation would be potentially unsafe?
options: Calling the mass a benign functional cyst while ignoring peritoneal implants
questions.explanation: Minimising clearly suspicious findings can delay diagnosis and treatment.
